🔥🇲🇽 <u>HUACHICOL FISCAL WAS BORN WITH THE PRIAN'S 2013 ENERGY REFORM: MORENA</u>

Before Peña Nieto's reform, only Pemex could import fuel. Then came the flood: more than 1,370 private import permits — including one for a company linked to the PAN's Ernesto Ruffo — and with them the smuggling and tax-evasion market the FGR is now dismantling.

AMLO asked for those permits to be revoked back in 2020.

"Ellos crearon el espacio y la manera de cómo importar hidrocarburos desde el extranjero," said Morena's Ariadna Montiel. The opposition that built the loophole now performs outrage about it.
banner: HUACHICOL FISCAL: BORN WITH 2013 PRIAN REFORM

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"A VISA DOESN'T DEFINE A MEXICAN": SHEINBAUM CALLS OUT US VISA CANCELLATIONS</u>

Revoking a visa without evidence of a crime is a political decision, President Sheinbaum said — interference, not security. If there's a crime to prosecute, present the proof and use the mechanisms, the way the US does when Mexico requests arrests on its territory.

And she drew the line on November: "México no es un tema para su elección; para su elección el tema son los problemas que tienen dentro de Estados Unidos, que son bastantes, no es México."

"En México deciden los mexicanos, no decide nadie más."
banner: SHEINBAUM: A VISA DOESN'T DEFINE MEXICANS

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>HARFUCH IN BUENOS AIRES: "NO CRIMINAL ORGANIZATION IS STRONGER THAN THE STATE"</u>

Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch presented Mexico's results at the 40th International Drug Control Conference (IDEC) in Buenos Aires: homicides at historic lows and more than 2,700 narco-labs dismantled under the National Security Strategy.

"Ninguna organización criminal es más fuerte que los Estados," he told the summit co-hosted by Argentina and the US.

Coordination without subordination — with the numbers on the table.
banner: HARFUCH: NO CARTEL STRONGER THAN THE STATE

text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>US SECRETLY DEPORTING MEXICANS TO GUATEMALA AND HONDURAS</u>

The Trump administration has been quietly flying Mexican deportees to third countries for months — hundreds of them — even though Mexico accepts the return of all its nationals. Two DHS officials confirmed it to CBS News: the goal is deterrence, sending people farther away from the US-Mexico border.

Mexico's Foreign Ministry was blunt: "The Government of Mexico accepts the return of all its nationals. It therefore rejects the deportation of Mexican nationals to third countries and has no such agreement in place."

WOLA's Adam Isacson called it what it is: "This is almost entirely punitive."
banner: US DEPORTS MEXICANS TO GUATEMALA, HONDURAS
